summary: Iteration 8 (Mingle Feed + Blocked members + Member view + regression). BACKEND 46/46 pytest passing on /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8_mingle_feed_blocks.py. Full coverage: (a) Mingle Feed gating — free-tier GET/POST /api/mingle/posts → 402; premium-without-profile → 403; empty body → 400; POST as member → 201 with space=='mingle', author.mingle==true, author.display_name=Mingle name, author.username==''; GET returns {items,next_cursor}. (b) Isolation — mingle post absent from /api/posts (all+following), /api/users/{author}/posts (posts+photos tabs), /api/me/saved after bookmark, /api/stories; GET /api/posts/{mid} → 403 for non-member and 200 with space='mingle' for member; main post creation still populates author.username. (c) Like/comment — B likes A's mingle post (201); B comments with mentions=[user_a] → server strips to mentions=[]; GET comments returns author.mingle=true, username=''; non-member like/comment → 403; A's /notifications entries for like+comment have mingle=true and actor.display_name='MingleB'. (d) Member view — /mingle/members/{me} is_me=true; after mutual 'interested', both sides see connection_id + conversation_id populated. (e) Block/unblock — /mingle/blocks lists blocked with display_name/photo_url/blocked_at; connections hide the pair both ways; B's mingle post gone from A's feed; GET /posts/{Bpid}→404 for A; POST /conversations/{conv}/messages both directions → 403 'You can't message this member'; /mingle/members/B → 404; discover excludes; DELETE /mingle/blocks/B → {unblocked:true}, second call → 404; after unblock connection is NOT restored (both sides empty), /mingle/members/B → 200 with connection_id=null, A can message again (201). (f) Regression — /mingle/me, PUT with 4 photos (persists photos + photo_url=photos[0]), /discover, /actions hi (creates conv + system greeting mentioning 'Single & Mingle'), /inbox, /connections, DELETE /mingle/connections/{id}, /report, /me/status, DELETE /mingle/me on throwaway; main /posts CRUD + mentioned_users resolve on MAIN comments; /notifications; /membership tier=premium. Settings → mingle-settings-blocked → mingle-blocked-screen renders. mingle-inbox-screen lists Nellie/Ava with Open chat / Interested / Pass buttons. action_items: Minor: Migrate remaining props.pointerEvents → style.pointerEvents to silence deprecation warning (still present from iter7; occurs when entering mingle screens).

Info (not a bug, verified): Because /api/mingle/block soft-deletes the connection row (mingle_connections.deleted_at) at block time, the review-request line 'Your Mingles does NOT regain the connection after unblock' is enforced by design. The one edge case worth documenting: after A unblocks B, A's prior 'interested' action toward B still exists in mingle_actions, so B stays out of A's /mingle/discover deck (matches the request's 'acceptable — verify instead that GET /mingle/members/B returns 200' — verified 200 with connection_id=null).

Info: Frontend selector count for post-share-* DOM nodes stayed >0 after leaving the discover screen for the mingle feed — traced to Expo Router keeping previous screens (home / discover) mounted in the stack. Visually confirmed via screenshot that mingle posts render NO share/bookmark buttons (post-card.tsx line 208-229 branches on isMingle), so this is purely stale DOM from prior tabs, not a bug.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_posts.enrich_posts() and comment_authors() both switch to mingle_summaries() for space=='mingle', giving authors mingle=true + username='' consistently across feed, detail, comments, and notifications — verified end-to-end.
MAIN_SPACE = {'space': {'$ne': 'mingle'}} is applied to /posts list, /users/{id}/posts, /me/saved — clean isolation guarantee.
get_post_or_404() gates mingle posts with both membership check (403) and blocked-pair check (returns 404 to blocker) — matches the request's asymmetric visibility semantics.

routes_mingle.unblock() deliberately only removes the block row — connection/action/conversation state is intentionally preserved (documented via docstring). Great intentional design choice for the 'unblock does NOT restore connection' requirement.
routes_mingle.block() soft-deletes mingle_connections in the same call, so /mingle/connections immediately hides the pair without needing a separate cleanup step.
routes_chat.send_message() uses mingle_blocked_ids(me) which is symmetric (returns any block in either direction) — that's why both A→B and B→A hit 403 while blocked. Correct.

routes_mingle.create_mingle_post() enforces require_premium + require_member and skips mentions entirely (mentions=[] hardcoded) — mention-suppression on mingle content is enforced at the create layer, not just enrich.

routes_posts.create_comment(): mentions = [] if is_mingle else resolve_selected_mentions(...) — mention-suppression enforced on comments too, matching the review-request 'comment mentions are ignored (mentions=[] even if body.mentions provided)'.

routes_activity.list_notifications() derives mingle-flag from BOTH n.type.startswith('mingle_') AND post_id in mingle posts, then swaps actor summary to mingle_summary — that's why like/comment notifications on a mingle post render with the Mingle display_name (verified in test_notifications_use_mingle_identity).

Blocked members: mingle-settings-blocked (settings row), mingle-blocked-screen, mingle-blocked-<user_id>, mingle-unblock-<user_id>. Member view: /mingle/member/[id] uses mingle-member-screen with mingle-member-hi / mingle-member-interested / mingle-member-message (existing). API contract clarifications: (1) POST /api/mingle/block soft-deletes both directions of mingle_connections, so 'restore after unblock' is impossible by design; (2) DELETE /api/mingle/blocks/{uid} returns {unblocked:true} — second call is 404; (3) mentioning users on a mingle comment silently drops the mentions server-side (mentions=[]); (4) get_post_or_404 for a mingle post: 403 for non-members (no profile), 404 for blocked-pair, 200 otherwise. To skip xdist for a stateful test file, run with `-n 0`.
